findings.section: Proposed fix / Claims vs findings ('bare directory')
findings.problem: The proposed fix classifies only ACP kinds edit/delete/move as file_change, but the opencode permission that actually produces a bare *directory* title (external_directory, title = parentDir) is mapped by opencode's toToolKind to kind "other" (no case for external_directory; default -> "other"). opencode's write/edit permission title is editTitle() = relativePath/filePath, i.e. a file path, not a directory. So the variant most likely matching the issue title ('carrying a bare directory path') would still render as a command approval after the patch, and the report's fake agent (kind "edit" + directory title via FAKE_ACP_PERMISSION_TITLE=dir) is a hybrid opencode never emits.
findings.evidence: /tmp/bb-reports/issues/1719/opencode-acp-tool.ts lines 38-70: toToolKind switch has cases bash/shell/webfetch/edit/apply_patch/patch/write/grep/glob/read/task and `default: return "other"`; no external_directory case. opencode-acp-permission.ts:142-143 external_directory title = description ?? command ?? parentDir; :157-170 write -> editTitle -> file path. Report's patch: ACP_FILE_CHANGE_TOOL_KINDS = new Set(["edit","delete","move"]).
findings.fix: State explicitly in Root cause / Proposed fix that opencode's external_directory permission arrives with kind "other" and is NOT covered by the kind-based classification; either extend the fix (e.g. classify by locations when kind is other/undefined and no command, or add a neutral/permission_grant subject) or downgrade the fix's claim to 'covers the write/edit variant only' and mark the 'bare directory' claim as only partially addressed.

findings.problem: The command `HOST=$(pnpm bb:dev machine list --json | python3 -c ...)` does not work as written: `pnpm bb:dev` prints turbo build banner lines to stdout before the JSON, so python's json.load fails with JSONDecodeError.
findings.evidence: Ran it verbatim in my worktree: `json.decoder.JSONDecodeError: Expecting value: line 2 column 1` with '• turbo 2.8.3 ...' preceding the JSON. `node packages/scripts/dist/commands/run-cli.js machine list --json` works.
findings.fix: Use `node packages/scripts/dist/commands/run-cli.js machine list --json` (after one `pnpm bb:dev` warm-up) or `bb machine list --json 2>/dev/null | sed -n '/^\[/,$p'`, and note the same for `thread spawn --json`.
